clue.text: Notes left for newsboys?

definitions.meaning: banknotes, the currency printed on paper
read literally, cash left out to pay the lads who deliver the papers

explanation.surface: Somebody leaves banknotes out as a tip for the paper boys.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: money that is for the papers, the sort left out for the boy who delivers them.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are currency printed on paper, and the cash owed for a newspaper round is the second, literal sense.

clue.text: Fork out about a pound for a dramatic show

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second here

parts.note: to fork out is to pay
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about spending a pound on a theatre ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a drama performed on stage, a dramatic show.

clue.text: Simple columnist taken round poetry circuit

indicators.note: taken round says the columnist's name is wrapped about the poetry word

parts.note: Peter Simple was the pen name of a long-running Daily Telegraph columnist
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, verse

explanation.surface: A humble newspaper writer is led around a poetry tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective but is half the name: Peter Simple was a famous satirical column in this very newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the boundary line all the way round, a circuit.

clue.text: The horseman recommended by the jury, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a jury may add a recommendation, such as mercy, to its verdict

explanation.surface: A cavalryman is singled out for praise by a panel of judges.
explanation.walkthrough: In court, a jury's added recommendation attached to a verdict is called a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both a person on horseback and a clause appended to a verdict or document.

clue.text: New policy about masculine games

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the single letter
new tells us the letters of policy are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: A new strategy is drawn up concerning men's sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges POLICY into OLYPIC, and 'about' puts that round M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic Games are the international sporting festival, so the adjective names those games.

clue.text: Add to the general confusion

indicators.note: confusion signals that the following word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something makes an already muddled situation worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the general confusion' reads as a phrase, but 'confusion' rearranges GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to increase it, to add to its size.

clue.text: Roguish artist turning to honoured companion

indicators.note: turning means the artist's letters are read the other way round

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A mischievous painter changes course towards a decorated friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means mischievous or knowingly playful, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: The girl I rebelled about

indicators.note: about says the rebelling word goes round the I

parts.note: to rise up is to rebel, so rose means rebelled

explanation.surface: A young woman says she revolted over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Judicial process in which net turnover is encouraging

indicators.note: in which says the second piece sits inside the court word

parts.note: a hearing is a session of a court

indicators.note: turnover means the word net is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A court case where the net business turnover looks promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net turnover' sounds like company accounts; 'turnover' is the reversal signal and 'in which' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartening lifts the spirits, giving encouragement.

clue.text: Rings up the Royal Society in fitting part of the West country

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the rings are read from the bottom

parts.note: O is a ring shape, so rings are Os

indicators.note: in places the society's letters inside the fitting word

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, the British science academy

explanation.surface: Someone phones the Royal Society in a suitable bit of England's south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings up' looks like phoning; in this down clue 'up' reverses OS to SO. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in the West Country of England, so it is one part of that region.

clue.text: Pungent help in which there's little credit

indicators.note: in which places the credit abbreviation inside the help word

parts.note: aid means help
CR is the short form, a little word, for credit

explanation.surface: Sharp-smelling assistance that earns hardly any thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a bitter, sharp smell or taste, so it means pungent.

clue.text: The main traffic route between China and Korea

definitions.text: The main traffic route between China and Korea

parts.words: The main traffic route between China and Korea
parts.note: the main is old poetic usage for the sea, and the shipping lanes between those two countries cross a particular one

explanation.surface: A geography question about the chief highway linking two Asian countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' suggests a principal road, but it is the poetic word for the sea, the body of water between China and the Korean peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellow Sea is the arm of the Pacific lying between mainland China and Korea, crossed by shipping.

clue.text: Unseemly fellow who lassoes a goblin?

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous goblin
a roper is one who ropes animals with a lasso

explanation.surface: A cowboy catching a little demon with a rope behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as IMP ROPER: someone who ropes an imp.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper conduct is unbecoming or indecent, that is, unseemly.

clue.text: A race that could go down in history

definitions.meaning: one contest in an athletics meeting

definitions.text: that could go down in history
definitions.meaning: a happening worth recording, a notable occurrence

explanation.surface: A sprint so memorable it will be remembered for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is both one competition in a sports programme and a significant historical occurrence.

clue.text: Dejected tyrant covering northern retreat

indicators.note: covering says the tyrant's letters go over and around the others

parts.note: a despot is a tyrant
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A depressed dictator shields his hideout in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondent means low in spirits and without hope, so downcast or dejected.

clue.text: Kind of fever that's unusual in Crete

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the two words are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A rare type of fever said to be uncommon on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges IN CRETE; 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric fever is the old name for typhoid, an intestinal fever, so the word names a kind of fever.

clue.text: As far as one can go in training?

definitions.text: As far as one can go in training?

parts.words: As far as one can go in training?
parts.note: training reads as practising but means travelling by train; the line ends at its last station

explanation.surface: An athlete asks about their limit in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' suggests exercise, but here it means going by train: a railhead is the end of a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A railhead is the point where a railway ends, the furthest a train journey can take you.

clue.text: Strange sea bird from the Orient

indicators.note: strange signals that the word next to it is altered in order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An odd seabird arrives from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange sea' reads as a description of the ocean, but 'Strange' is the anagram signal working on the word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means belonging to the East, the lands of Asia once called the Orient.

clue.text: The last dock the captured buccaneer saw?

definitions.text: The last dock the captured buccaneer saw?

parts.words: The last dock the captured buccaneer saw?
parts.note: pirates were hanged at a named dock on the Thames at Wapping, so its name describes the final stage of their lives

explanation.surface: A question about the final harbour a seized pirate saw.
explanation.walkthrough: Execution Dock in Wapping, east London, is where pirates were hanged, so the dock's name is the fate that awaited them.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution is the carrying out of a death sentence, which is what awaited a captured pirate at Execution Dock.

clue.text: Turn right up to see the scope offered

indicators.note: turn means the following pair of pieces is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
to view is to see

explanation.surface: Turn up on the right to look over the range on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses R and UP together, giving PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the range of authority or concern, its scope.

clue.text: Frankly having nobody to substitute in the field

definitions.meaning: speaking openly and holding nothing back

definitions.text: having nobody to substitute in the field
definitions.meaning: literally lacking a substitute player for the team

explanation.surface: To be honest, the team has no replacements on the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: A reserve is a substitute player, so a team without one is literally without reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without reserve means openly and candidly, and a team short of substitutes literally lacks a reserve.

clue.text: Entreat redress for a coarse fabric

indicators.note: redress, read as re-dress, says the letters are put in new order

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for compensation over some rough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redress' looks like compensation but is read as dress again, rearranging ENTREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratteen is an old thick woollen cloth, a coarse fabric.

clue.text: See 20
Magnetic personality who ran George III's parliament

definitions.meaning: a compass needle points to the magnetic pole

definitions.text: personality who ran George III's parliament
definitions.meaning: Lord ... was Prime Minister under King George III, from 1770 to 1782

explanation.surface: A charismatic figure who led the government of an 18th-century king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magnetic personality' reads as a charmer, but the clue splits there: magnetic north, and Lord North, the British Prime Minister who lost the American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic north is the direction a compass shows, and Lord North led King George III's ministry.

clue.text: Didn't walk round the Wild West show

parts.note: rode, travelled on horseback rather than on foot
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cowboy rode round the frontier exhibition rather than walking it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a display of cowboy skills such as bronco riding, a Wild West show.

clue.text: Elegant individual who never errs in a flute composition

indicators.note: in says the person and saint go inside the rearranged flute
composition signals that flute's letters are composed anew

parts.note: a means one, a single individual
ST, for saint, a person held to be without sin

explanation.surface: A refined musician who never plays a wrong note in a flute piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' is the anagram signal, and 'in' puts a saint, the individual who never errs, inside after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means showing good judgement in style, so refined or elegant.

clue.text: Fix me up with a place for the night

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means me is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
a bed is where one sleeps at night

explanation.surface: A traveller asks to be found somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix me up' sounds like arranging; 'up' turns ME to EM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed is to set something firmly in a surrounding mass, to fix it in place.

clue.text: Far from happy little boy?

definitions.meaning: Little Boy ... is a nursery rhyme character

explanation.surface: A small child who is clearly miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Boy Blue is the nursery-rhyme boy who should come blow his horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means low in spirits, and it completes the nursery-rhyme name Little Boy Blue.

clue.text: The effort that first took Captain Cook to the Pacific

definitions.text: that first took Captain Cook to the Pacific

explanation.surface: A tribute to the attempt that carried Cook to the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: HM Bark Endeavour was the ship of James Cook's first Pacific voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is a serious attempt, and HMS Endeavour was the vessel of Cook's first voyage.

clue.text: The fish our nationalised lines need badly

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railways when they were state-owned
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A complaint that state railways are in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail was the nationalised railway company of Great Britain until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: An implement to behold in retrospect

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in retrospect, looking back, means the word for behold is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A device worth looking back on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is a hand instrument for doing work, an implement.

clue.text: Those who come between nine and eleven to take the floor

parts.note: at ten o'clock, the hour between nine and eleven
to take the floor is to get up and dance

explanation.surface: Guests arrive at a set hour to join the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as AT TEN plus DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the number of people present, the body of those who turn up.
